question: All Helicobacter pylori strains carry the cagA pathogenicity island, which is why H. pylori infection invariably progresses to gastric adenocarcinoma.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is false. The cagA gene is present in a subset of strains, not all. CagA-positive strains (which predominate in Asia) carry higher cancer risk via Ras–ERK oncogenic signalling, but infection does not invariably progress to cancer — host immunity and other factors determine outcome.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this is false on both counts. Only a subset of H. pylori strains carry cagA (though CagA-positive strains predominate in South and East Asia). Even among CagA-positive infections, progression to cancer is not inevitable — most infected individuals never develop malignancy.
